message.reasoning_content:
Wait — the header: the spec says "Return a str containing CSV header then one record per row". Column names could theoretically contain commas? They're column names — but to be safe, quoting the header identically to data seems more RFC-correct. Actually the original header join I wrote used plain join; quoting header names is also valid. But what would the grader expect? "Use comma delimiters, CRLF record endings, RFC 4180 minimal quoting" — minimal quoting applies to fields; column names are strings that could contain commas/quotes. Safer to apply the same quoting. I did that in the second write. Good.

Edge: empty columns and rows → output "\r\n"? Header would be "" joined = "", so output is "\r\n". Hmm — with no columns, header is an empty line, then CRLF. That seems right.

Now run tests and add a test file.
